utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: There is one question that Mr. Topolski didn't put to the witness and I'd like to put it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure Mr. Mansfield won't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jasovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I remind you again of the affirmation you made at the commencement of your evidence which still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Powles will ask you something as the first question this afternoon. Yes, Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Powles:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jasovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jasovic. My name is Steven Powles, and I am the co-counsel for Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, I'm glad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a couple of questions that Mr. Topolski omitted to put to you yesterday afternoon so I intend to put them to you now. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the good cop/bad cop method of interrogation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good cop/bad cop. I don't know. I know for myself that I'm a good cop, that I've performed my tasks honestly and honourable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly, Mr. Jasovic, it's where during an interrogation one interrogator is nice to the witness and the other one is rather nasty. Just to assure you, when it comes to Mr. Topolski and myself I'm the good cop. I'm going to be relatively gentle will you. The first question is: Do you know Adem Ibrahimi?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding names -- could you tell me where he was from?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you. He was the deputy chief of the directorate in the secretariat of interior, SUP, for the Ferizaj region. From 1970 to 1989 he was in the SUP in Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This name is known to me, but they used to call him Adem Goga [phoen]. He was deputy of public security in Urosevac. Now he's retired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So he was in the SUP in Ferizaj at the same time as you, given that you started there around 1980.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1st of July, 7 -- 1970 from 1st May of 1981 I was appointed assistant commander of the police station in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're familiar with this man and you were in the SUP with him at the same time in Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in the public security whereas Mr. Adem Goga Ibrahimi worked in state security service. And state security is separated from public security service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So thank you very much, Mr. Jasovic. I promised I would be gentle and I was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Powles. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, compared to yesterday, this was great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's encouraging you, Mr. Mansfield, to follow example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure where that leaves me, but we'll ask later. Cross-examined by Mr. Mansfield:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jasovic. I represent, along with my co-counsel Mr. Karim Khan, Fatmir Limaj who sits behind. I want to ask -- before dealing with a specific person who you dealt with but who was referred to yesterday as X in public session, but before dealing with him, I just want to follow through on some topics from yesterday. First of all, during the 1990s, were you aware that the police station in Ferizaj where you worked had a reputation in the community for brutality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not known to me. I know nothing about that, concerning individuals taking a brutal attitude towards Albanians, if that's what you meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. It's a bit wider than that. The question was whether you were aware that the police station in which you worked in the 1990s had a reputation in the community for brutality. Now, were you aware of that reputation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not known to me because from 1986, I worked as a plainclothes policeman, as an inspector. I was on the third floor, whereas -- I can't remember now, but the police department was on the second floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come to this, but you associated with members of the Albanian community. You visited some of them in their homes, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to visit Albanians, but these visits don't mean to be social as friends or acquaintances. I used to visit in an official capacity from 1975 to 1981. Our patrols would be -- would comprise leader -- patrol leader and assistant patrol leader, and since I was a young cop, leaders of patrols used to be Albanians. Our police station in Stimlje numbered seven to eight staff, policemen, and there were two or three Serbs employed in the policemen, I mean. There were three of us. Subsequently, one was transferred from Stimlje police station to the Urosevac police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What years did I specify in the question I asked you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned the year 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask the question again, therefore. I'm not asking you about the 1975 period or the 1981 period. I'm asking you about the 1990s, the decade. In that period, you visited Albanians who were known to you in their homes, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be as concrete as possible, I visited most Albanian homes as a policeman while I used to work in Stimlje as a policeman with my Albanian colleague. In the 1990s, I used to, given my father-in-law is in a village there, I used to visit him and his neighbours. I don't want to mention their names. And that was all. I used to visit homes of Albanian colleagues from the SUP of Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to mention his name at the moment at all, obviously, in public. You visited the home of X, who we're coming to later, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to go there as a policeman while I was in the 1975, 1981 period while I worked in the Stimlje police station. His father or, Person A, I used to meet in Urosevac and Stimlje. I happened upon him in cafes, in the streets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the question I'm posing at the moment is: I suggest that you full well knew that the reputation of the police station amongst the Albanian community was one of brutality. You knew that, didn't you? That was the reputation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. I did not know about that. I wasn't the commander of police station, neither the head of police department. Whatever they did policemen had to account for to their immediate superiors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I suppose are you saying within the police station itself there wasn't a canteen or somewhere where you mixed with other people from other floors, you had conversations, you socialised? Are you saying you didn't know what was going on on other floors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know. I did my work in my office on the third floor. I didn't -- didn't have a practice of walking around to be able to know what used to happen on the second floor, for the second floor housed a number of offices, two or three of them heads of security. But the duty officer was on the ground floor and the office of the commander of the police station, chief, their assistant -- deputy and several assistants. I don't know the number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was in the basement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the basement. Not in the basement. Duty officers' quarters. Not in the basement, on the ground floor. So chief of shift and the duty officers, where I got out of uniform. There were four or five policemen. I'm not sure what happened then -- there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you still attempting to cover up for what was going on in that police station by feigning ignorance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, sir, I come here voluntarily, and I took a solemn declaration. And I'm telling the truth, the whole truth, and the truth will prevail sooner or later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the second topic in relation to this area, were you aware in the 1990s that in addition to the reputation of the police station that you personally had a reputation amongst the Albanian community of being a brutal police officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. This is not true. I can prove that. I have even today a large number of friends among the Albanian community. And they themselves told me, "Dragan, go there to prove the truth. Go there to The Hague," for me to come here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And none of these friends were able to tell you that the reputation that you had and the police station had was one of brutality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My friends could not tell me because this is not true. I did not do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you're missing the point for the moment. We'll come to whether you did it in a moment in relation to somebody in particular, who is very relevant to these proceedings. I'm dealing with the reputation that you had. And I'm suggesting to you you cannot possibly have been unaware of the reputation that you had in the 1990s, can you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for myself that I had a good reputation among the Albanians. This is what I stick to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you in this same period of time as a result of that same period of time, I'm bringing it forward to last year, 2004, I believe was the first time in which you were interviewed by someone on behalf of this Tribunal, 2004. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 2004, the office of the ICTY in Belgrade, I believe it was in May, 12th of May, interviewed me. Mr. Ole. I don't know his surname, but he hails from Finland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask this in stages. Now, I'm dealing with the period before May 2004. Had you become aware of reports by organisations indicating brutality at the police station in Ferizaj? In other words, publications mentioned to you yesterday which suggested there was evidence of large numbers of people passing through your police station and being brutalised. Now, were you aware of a single report like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this report. I did not follow the situation. I was not interested in it because in concrete terms, I know for a fact that I worked, performed my duties in accordance with laws and the constitution of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate you will repeat that, but the question is whether you became aware between 1999 and 2004 of public reports being made, substantial allegations of torture in your police station. Now, did you become aware of those?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you recently I did not learn about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because if you had, you would have been interested. Since you say you did no wrong, you would have been interested, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not learn about that. I wouldn't have taken an interest in that even if I had. This is all the same to me, but I'm telling you I did not learn about that. And even if I had, I wouldn't make an effort to seek these reports, because I know that I did not commit any crimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before 2004, had anybody approached you to interview you or question you about these suggestions to see if you knew anything about it? Had anybody approached you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning which topic? I did not understand your question. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll make it simple. Between 1999 and 2004, did anyone on behalf of an authority either in Serbia or in Kosovo approach you to find out whether you could assist with allegations being made about torture from your police station -- in your police station? Did anybody approach you to ask you questions about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, sir, if anybody approached regarding that in the secretariat there is the head of the secretariat. I don't know if he was approach. I had my area of operations. There was no need for me, and this would go against the procedure of the SUP. Bogoljub Janicevic was chief of the secretariat. I cannot tell you whether anybody approached him or not. I can tell you that nobody has approached me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was about you, so kindly focus on the question. So you're saying nobody has approached you before 2004. Now, I want to come to 2004. When you met with the investigators in 2004, did anybody at that stage ask you about these allegations before you made a statement to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. When you were seen in 2004 on behalf of the ICTY and an interview you've mentioned in May was conducted with you, did anybody at that stage raise with you the question of brutality in your police station and the question of whether you had, yourself, been brutal to anyone in particular?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the police station? You mean the SUP Urosevac, dislocated in Leskovac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll be more precise. Did anybody before taking the statement dealing with events in 1998 ask you -- 1998, 1999 -- about any allegations of brutality in the Ferizaj police station during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you warned in any way about the risk of incrimination, incriminating yourself in areas like this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't warned by anybody, because they had no grounds to warn me because I performed my tasks and duties in accordance with law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to come, therefore, to this year for that very reason. When you arrived in The Hague as was indicated a day or so ago over the Easter period, the 2nd, 3rd, 4th of April this year, you were interviewed again, weren't you, by the representatives of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which date? On which date, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we have a supplemental statement or information sheet with a date of the 4th of April. I understand, in fact, it may be the 3rd of April as well, but it's somewhere in that period you were interviewed here in The Hague before you gave evidence.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interview on the premises of the Tribunal was conducted by Mr. Black I think was his name. It was on Saturday, Sunday, and Monday, the 2nd, the 3rd, and the 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 2nd, the 3rd, and the 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was a Saturday, Sunday, and a Monday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, next question: Did anybody in that period of time tell you - that is anyone on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor - that they were collecting evidence in Kosovo on the very same days, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th, about your activities in relation to people who had been taken to the Ferizaj police station? Did anyone tell you that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me that. My mobile is out of order. I did not contact anyone. I only called my family at home using the telephone in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may have misunderstood. The point I'm making to you concerns another remarkable coincidence. One was pointed out yesterday. This is another one. I want to know whether while you were being interviewed in The Hague by the Office of the Prosecutor that anybody on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor told you that the Office of the Prosecutor had marshaled or collected information and statements from witnesses in Kosovo about you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me that. This is the first time I've heard such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take just a moment on this topic because you were asked yesterday about three particular people, and so far as the transcript is concerned, you were indicating that you either didn't know or couldn't remember these individuals. So I want to ask you again about the individuals who were giving statements over the same weekend that you were being interviewed here. Now, I'm going to ask them one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And for these purposes, Your Honours, we've had bundles of statements prepared in relation to these witnesses. So Your Honours have copies of the named individuals. And then in due time I'll ask for the witness to have the Albanian version. May I just hand them up. I think Mr. Whiting kindly gave us some copies this morning. May I just check that the statement on the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I'll give you an Albanian set now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Presumably these are B/C/S or are they in fact in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The ones for the witness are in Albanian. The rest are English statements and translations. And -- I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If these are the same that were provided yesterday they're in B/C/S. I'm not sure if it is a different copy. The Serbian language as opposed to the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether the bundle I was given today is exactly the same as the one yesterday. I understand it is, yes. Thank you. Can I just check that the statement on the top in English should read -- we tried to do it in date order, Afrim Mustafa. It should be the one on the top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you about that name first of all. He was seen on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd of April this year in Pristina. Do you know that name, first of all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that name. As I said, I cannot recall first and last names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Well, it's in the light of that answer that would you please look at statements that are behind the statement that he gave to the ICTY, which includes an English translation, I suggest, of a statement that you took on the 17th of January, 1999. Now, would you look, please, at the -- a copy that you have there of the original statement.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the 17th, the 16th of January. This is something about an interview with Afrim Mustafa. I don't know whether you have the date the 16th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It begins with the 16th, and it -- there is writing at the end of it on our -- on our second page, possibly your only page, of the 17th. So it's in that period. But what I want to identify from you first of all: This is a statement you took in January 1999, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. Can I see the signature of the person taking the statement? I don't have the second page here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we -- I'm only being able to operate on what we are given. We are led to believe that this is a statement taken by you and your colleague in the same way as all the statements you went through, in the sense of what's on the face of the document, you went through yesterday. Could I ask if there's a copy which has this witness's signature upon it. If there isn't, I can't take it further for the moment. It looks as though there may not be.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I don't have one here. We'll make inquiries to see if we can find that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, can we proceed for the moment on the basis of the information that we've been provided with, that this was a statement taken by you in January 1999. May we just proceed on that basis for the moment. And plainly, if it then transpires that it isn't your signature on that, then it will have to be qualified. The question I have for you, assuming you did take this statement, as we're led to believe you did, is looking at the statement, I want to ask you how this person ever came to be in the Ferizaj police station.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In connection with this statement, I don't know whether I took the statement together with my colleague. I don't know. So I would not like to discuss it. I do not remember this name. If you find the second part, then there won't be any problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just bear with me for a moment. I'm sure the second part will be found. Our English version certainly has your name attached to it. You see, if you look at the introductory paragraph, there's no indication of why this person was at the police station and what it was that he was supposed to be there for. Do you follow? And I want to know, if you can help us, how it came to be that he was at the police station. He was about 16 at the time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, first, as I said, I cannot discuss this. If I see that it was my colleague and me who took the statement, then I can talk about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, this is the young man -- it was put to you yesterday and I'm not going to do it in detail. This is the young man who suggests, no longer so young, that he was subjected to forms of electrocution in order to get him to talk. Do you remember that being put to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember yesterday the name of Afrim Mustafa was mentioned. But I don't know this young man. I can't remember such a young man. I'm sure all this is fabricated. There was no torture used, no electricity was used. There was no physical maltreatment. There was no reason to do that to a 16-year-old child. Why was he brought in? I'm sure I didn't do it, but perhaps the police found him in a suspicious place. That's an assumption only. I see that he is from the village of Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Is that enough to bring you in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you're welcome --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not enough, but not only Afrim Mustafa but there was nobody against whom crimes were perpetrated. I don't know why he was brought in. The policeman who authorised officials have their senior officer, their commander, their assistants, and if they brought somebody in, I'm sure they -- they checked with their superior officer about that. It wasn't my duty to question policemen as to why they had brought somebody in. I cannot remember a person like this. But what you say about torture, I can say that not only he but nobody was tortured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, if he's brought in for a specific reason, you would expect that to be in the introductory paragraph, brought in because of acting in a suspicious way or suspected of carrying weapons or whatever it happens to be. You would expect that to be there, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that again, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would expect the introductory paragraph to indicate why they've been brought in.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not the practice to put in why somebody had been brought in. The date was probably the 16th of January, 1999, when there was armed fighting going on in the Racak area. I really couldn't tell you the reason why he was brought in, because it was the police who did that. Whenever a police officer brought somebody into the police station in Urosevac, they were duty-bound to draw up an official note for the commander of the police station explaining why this person had been brought in. But it was not my duty to put this into the official note or the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been a massacre in Racak committed by Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that because I was not in Racak. It is my opinion that there was no massacre, but I was not there in the village of Racak. You can ask the chief of the SUP in Urosevac, Bogoljub Janicevic about that. He was my chief, and he was also a political official.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you as an ordinary person living --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you -- I'm telling you that there was no massacre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Even today, despite international recognition that there was a massacre there, you're still not prepared to accept it, are you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot accept it because it's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to pass to the second individual, please. We may have the same problem, I'm afraid. I have to deal with what I've been given. But on this occasion, the name is Muhadin Xheladini.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muhadin Xheladini. I can see it written here. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you know that name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that person. I know about the statement. I can see that it was signed by Momcilo Sparavalo and myself, although the copy's poor. I don't know the person but he was interviewed. An informative interview was conducted with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore the position is that so far as this one is concerned -- this is the one who yesterday was put to you as a name and as somebody who, again, was subjected to force in your police station. He'd seen blood on the floor and so on. Do you remember that being put to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About Afrim Mustafa -- well, no. My brain is not a computer. I can't recall all the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. This is only yesterday I'm asking you about. But I'll continue. Can you tell me why --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you I don't remember. I do apologise, but I cannot recall that. I cannot remember the first and last name. Maybe it was mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you blotted these names out because, in fact, you know full well that these were victims of your police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct that I've blotted these names out. To me, every person is the same whether his name be Muhadin, Dragan, Bajram or whether he comes from some other country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you again. How did this man come to be interviewed by you? And again to make it clear, these statements are mostly about the KLA.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The KLA is mentioned in the statements. I don't know whether the person came to the secretariat of their own accord or whether they were brought in by policemen. I can't remember that, because it's been -- it's been more than six years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you it's important for what we're coming to in a moment. There are two categories of people. There are those who you bring in, and I suggest these are people who have been brought in by police to your police station and who are made to speak; that's one category. The other category are people who are friendly towards you and to whom you have to exercise no force. Those are the two main categories, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn to the last statement. Yesterday, I think the name was inadvertently misrepresented to you, but I want to correct it now. The third name you will see on the statement that you have is Shemsi Emini.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shemsi Emini.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I think on your copy you will see again you've dealt with this one, too, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement was taken by Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo and me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once again, can you give any enlightenment as to how this person ends up in your police station talking about the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this person came in of their own accord or whether they were brought in by policemen. This person is from the village of Racak. It's possible he was brought in by policemen from Stimlje police station, but I don't know. I don't know where this person was found, whether in Stimlje or Urosevac. I really couldn't say. It's possible, but I don't know. I don't know where they were found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, I want to suggest to you that with the reputation of your police station, people are not going to be queueing up to come to your police station. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Urosevac, there are four police stations, Urosevac, Stimlje, Strpce, and Kacanik. I don't know which one you're referring to. Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The one where you took this statement.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I don't know whether this person was brought in. I don't know where this person was found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, without this signature on this statement, I dare say you'd have said you had nothing to do with him. The fact is you did have something is to do with this individual, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, even if there had been no signature, it's enough for me to see my name here and I accept every statement that bears my name even without a signature. I accept that I interviewed Emini Shemsi, Shemsi Emini. I'm not sure whether I've been clear enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's the one who suggests that he was beaten with baseball bats or objects similar to baseball bats. Now, you did have objects similar to baseball bats in your office, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had nothing like that. I didn't even have a truncheon, let alone baseball bats or sticks. It's not true that there were objects like that in office 59, even though the gentleman yesterday mentioned different numbers until we arrived at 59.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in light of that answer, I want to come to another individual, but I'll do it in public for the moment, but please be careful about mentioning his name. If I call him X, you do appreciate who we're talking about, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Person X, you mean from yesterday's session?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all right. I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, first question on this is: Do you know what he has told this Tribunal about you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you'll believe me, but I'm telling you quite sincerely that I did not follow those proceedings at all, and I don't know what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to round that off, does it mean, therefore, over the Easter weekend, that is Saturday, Sunday, Monday, no one from the Office of the Prosecutor asked you about allegations that he has made about you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During Easter, I don't know what date it was because I had calls both from the assistants here and from Belgrade. I don't know who called me, all the people who called me. But none of them mentioned the name of Person X. He was not mentioned at all, and I wasn't interested in what he was saying, except that from the Hague Tribunal they told me I'd be coming here on the 14th, the 25th, the 28th. That was what we talked about on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I don't know if it's helpful at all, but the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th of April, that wasn't the Easter weekend. That could be part of the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's -- I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not so much the period. I mean the period of time when your here. I think you recognise that, and what you're saying is that no one in the period of time that you were here being interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor asked you about allegations being made by the witness X against you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat it, please, the dates that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The dates I'll leave to one side for the moment. The days that you were here being interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor before you gave evidence, which you indicated was a Saturday, a Sunday, and a Monday in April, and we have your statement dated the 4th of April, no one from the Office of the Prosecutor in that period, because it's long after the time that X gave evidence, asked you about the allegations that he made about you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over the weekend -- I didn't understand you. Are you referring to the weekend on the premises of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe so, yes. You were here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: case. Should I tell you everything? I don't know whether I've been clear enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pause for a moment, because I've asked you to be careful about the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Please could that be redacted. It's two lines --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please listen to the question. We can be much quicker to you do. The question is a very simple one.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'd be happy to finish more quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is the answer to the question. The question is: Did anyone from the Office of the Prosecutor before you gave evidence tell you of allegations against you by the witness X?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me, none of the people I talked to. Mr. Black didn't tell me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you to deal with this -- this particular person. I'm going to do it carefully, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Redaction has been ordered, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I'm much obliged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to start with the father of X. How long had you known his father by 1998/1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had known him at least for 20 years. I couldn't tell you whether it's 18 or 22, but take the mean of 20 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the father yesterday as a good friend. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm not ashamed of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated also that you had met him, that is the father, at the beginning of 1998.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I could not remember which month. It was cold. Maybe January, February, March. Had I known that I would be coming here, I would have written down the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you carefully because when I come to X himself, you've given different versions of your knowledge of him, and I'm come to that in a moment. That's why I'm going carefully. Now, when you saw the father, you would go to the home of the father for a drink from time to time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said. And to follow up on what I said earlier, I used to visit his father's house from 1975 to 1981. After that, I would go for a drink in a cafe. This was mostly in a cafe in Stimlje and in Urosevac. And in the period 1975 to 1981, I visited on several occasions in my capacity as policeman while patrolling that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to pause for a moment because I want to identify with you. You indicated yesterday that there was a register, and on that register your one registered informant would be placed; is that right? As well as others, presumably.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to dub that connection, person B, as I said. This was the only registered connection that I had or contact. I will dub that person "Person B" about whom I said yesterday or the day before yesterday, something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to deal with that person for a moment. That person would give you information from time to time. Where was the information recorded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- we would prepare official notes or briefs. How -- what do you mean how it was recorded?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I want to try and identify, because so far it hasn't been identified, the registered informant. I'm just dealing with that person for the moment you said would give you information from time to time, might be tasked to give you and get certain information. Where would you record the information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not clear to me again. You mean during the conversation or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a very simple question. Where did you record the information that he gave you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of an interview -- if you mean where we met -- I'm not clear whether this translation is clear to me. Can you -- I apologise, but this is not clear to me what goes through the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what document would you record the information he gave you over the course of two years?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After an interview was completed, sometimes that person would submit to me a note in his handwriting. Sometimes I would take down notes. But I told you yesterday that we would meet in discreet places outside Urosevac. Later on, I would prepare official notes or briefs depending on the nature of information obtained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do any of the notes, either official or unofficial, recording his information still exist?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some notes exist. I tried, but I'm not sure whether this was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. taken out from the secretariat in Urosevac, because we had to abandon it within 24 hours. I tried, and I will keep trying to find something in our secretariat, because our offices are very cramped. We moved to smaller premises. Some 30-odd officers work in a couple of offices. It is possible that official notes or briefs exist somewhere in Leskovac, but I'm not sure because quite a lot of material was left behind in the Urosevac secretariat, and I'm not aware that this is doable, but if they have not been destroyed, there could be some notes remaining in the office number 59 on third floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you at any stage been asked to identify any notes of information provided by the registered informant?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was required? Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been asked at any time by the Office of the Prosecutor to identify any reports, notes, whatever, where the information which the registered informant can be found?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which Prosecution officer would require that or ask that. The question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you whether you're purposefully being difficult about these questions. They are very simple. I will ask it again for the last time. Have you been asked by anyone on behalf of the Prosecutor to identify any records which indicate information provided by the registered informant?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Mr. Black or -- I don't know who you're referring to. I apologise. I do not have any intentions in this regard. I am not ill-intentioned, but I don't know which Prosecution do you refer to. I don't know. Do you mean the ICTY's office in Belgrade or maybe Mr. Black here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't want to answer questions, do you, on this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I want to answer questions, but I'm not sure whether you're talking about my conversations in Belgrade or here. Here in the Tribunal, regarding registered contact, Mr. Black and others in Belgrade did not know of the name of that registered informant, because nobody asked me that in Belgrade. Here, after I've completed my interview with Mr. Black, I mentioned this registered informant. Regarding official notes, I told him that there are with regard to attacks against certain houses. But I could not tell him whether official notes existed in our premises because I did not pay attention to it. The people from the Tribunal announced that the topic of discussion will be Lapusnik. I can check this back in Leskovac, but the people in Belgrade never asked me about the registered informant. I'm not sure whether I'm clear. And I said to Mr. Black, "I don't know what kind of official notes I have still." I showed him one official note, and then for the rest I said I didn't know. I'm not sure whether this has been taken from the offices of the secretariat in Urosevac, and it is not that I don't want to answer. They found me on several occasions. I went to Belgrade on several occasions. I'm not sure whether you're referring to my dealings with them in Belgrade or here in The Hague. Because Mr. Black, after I've told him about the registered informant, he asked me whether you have something written down, any records, notes concerning that informant. Am I being clear now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You finally got to the answer that you did indicate that there might be something written down. You see, we're trying to track down sources of information, what information was had. That's why you're here. You do appreciate that, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear to me. There must be notes. I'm not sure whether they are now in Leskovac or whether they were left behind in the Urosevac building, because quite a lot of material was left behind in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, besides your agency, did other agencies of the Serbian state have registered informants as well, the UDBA and KOS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding other services most probably, yes, but I can't tell you for the other services whether they had or not, because yesterday, also I said because of confidentiality, for reasons of conspiracy, I did not know whether my immediate colleagues had any informants or not. Although if my colleague were to say, "I have an informant," I would not know the identity of that informer, the name, surname, vital statistics. For other secretariats, most probably, yes, depending on the authorised officials, because for our informant to be registered, the senior officer must be addressed with that issue. So criminal investigation department, the chief of that department would be contacted by us, approached by us, because of the type of -- confidential type of information. We had to preclude any leaks. So the superior officer kept the register of such informants. In concrete terms, in our department the chief of the criminal investigation department for general crime and white office crime that was kept by that person and the chief of the secretariat appointed Branko Debeljkovic who kept the register. He knows best how many people and which people were registered there. Concerning other secretariats, I don't know. If the chief trust as policeman, he could appoint that person to keep the register. This is at the discretion of the chief of the secretariat to determine who will keep such records of registered informers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move to another category, that is non-registered. If you had a friendly operative, was a list kept of those people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no list. Friendly contacts are people you get in contact on a daily basis, whether a Serb, a Roma, or Albanian, et cetera, et cetera. How shall I put it? Socialising, social contacts. Whether at a cafe, at home, or where else. Such a friendly contact may say, "I heard about this so-and-so case." But this friendly contact does not necessarily concern only terrorism. Or maybe a friendly contact can be the street sweeper that I socialise with on occasion. And such people, they provide information on a friendly basis. They are not forced to provide information -- although nobody was forced to provide information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to X and his family, they fall into that category, don't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. He is a friend of mine, not a friendly contact. With the person X, I know him -- I've known him for a long time but did not socialise with him, whereas with his father I socialised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'll dealing with his father for the moment. His father fell into the category, after 20 years, of a friendly operative, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Really, this photograph is really poor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just happened to notice looking at the monitors outside that this photograph has been zoomed in on the cameras in the public gallery. I don't know if that's going to lead to a problem, but perhaps that shouldn't be done or we should go into private session. I don't know what the appropriate solution is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think to make the point that I have to make in the light of the answer is private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of the hour, we will have the first break now. As there are redactions, the break will need to be for half an hour. There is one order which I must sign before I leave the courtroom, one further order. We will now adjourn, resuming at ten past four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May we resume in private session just for a short time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so it's shown I'm not going to mention any names, but you have been shown a photograph in which you have managed to identify X's father amongst a group of people you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Person X, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. Just let me finish. I'm just doing a summary for the benefit of public record. X's father amongst a group of Serbs in a hunting party, and you have named one, so far as you can remember. Is that a fair summary of what we've just dealt with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It's correct about the name of X's father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move on, please, to X himself. Before July the 18th, when you interviewed him about the kidnapping of his father, had you ever met him? That is X himself.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. Yes, I had met him before the 18th of July, but certainly not in 1997 or 1998. Whether it was three, four, five or six years before I can't be sure, because as I said previously, I knew him but he was not a person I sat with in cafes or in any other place, while I did do so with his father. Let me repeat. I don't know when it was that I met him before. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to ask you this smaller detail about X before we go further. You told the Office of the Prosecutor last year when you were first interviewed that you didn't know X personally, "But I knew who he was." And then when you were interviewed this year, you changed that and you said that you did know X personally. What's the explanation for the change, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain it. It was probably a misinterpretation. I signed a statement that was in English. I didn't read it in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, I want to then indicate to you what X has said about you. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I follow, and I'd really like to hear it as I didn't follow the proceedings when he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that others may follow if they wish, it is a transcript from Day 24, so it's some time ago. It's page 37. And it's dealing with his visit to your police station on July the 18th. Now, for these purposes you may like to have in front of you the document that arises out of this. It is, in fact, under seal. Prosecution Exhibit No. 210 at tab 26. So if you could have that in front of you, please. It's tab 26. P210 is the document that arises, but I want to deal with the lead-up to this. So do you have that in front much you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have his statement in front of me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't need to read it for the moment because I'm going to deal with what he says happened and how this came about and ask for your observations about this. I'm going to summarise the first part. He told this Tribunal that he'd been stopped at a checkpoint with his uncle in his uncle's car and that he was taken -- they were taken together to your police station. Now, on that I've just summarised. That's how it starts. Had you ordered that he be brought into the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct that I ordered he be brought in. I knew him. I didn't need him there, because how could I know who the patrol would find at the checkpoint and bring in?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And with regard to this particular witness, please understand I'm wanting your help about what he's saying. So you say you didn't order him to be brought in. And then he's asked what happened when he got to the police station with his uncle. And then -- I'm now going to quote what he's actually said here. "We went there to SUP, to the police headquarters. We were left there for one or two hours in an office, then they were taken to the office of an inspector. His name was Dragan Jasovic." Now, do you know whether they were held for one or two hours first, before they got to your office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not aware of that, that they were detained there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I know it's a little time ago, but was he in the company -- in relation to this document I've just asked you to look at, was he in the company of his uncle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if I read the statement. I don't know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to save time here because you can read the statement. We are going to look at it in a moment. Not in a lot of detail. There's no reference in the statement to his uncle. Do you follow? Would you accept that from me for the moment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it isn't mentioned in the statement, then he probably didn't tell me that he had been brought in with his uncle, because I know him. It's possible I knew his uncle from the time when I went to visit there between 1975 and 1981. I may know him by sight, although I can't recall his face now. They may have been together or they might not have been. He didn't tell me anything about this in the interview. Had he told me this, then certainly I would have received both of them in my office. I would have told them to call his uncle in as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the question I'm asking you is was his uncle with him when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Because that is what he's saying. "We were taken to the offers of an inspector." Your recollection is no uncle. Now I'll move on. The question he's next asked in this Tribunal: "Now, this person Dragan Jasovic, have you ever met this person before?" Answer: "I had not met him before personally, but I had seen him in Stimlje and sometimes in Ferizaj." Now, just pausing there. There's more to come. That's not true, is it? He did know you personally, or you had met him, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I don't know when I got to know him, but it was sometime between 1975 and 1981. And what he said here, that I never went to his house, maybe he was afraid to provide this information. I don't know what he meant by it, I can't say. But I'm certain that he knew me and that he saw me in his house in the period between 1975 and 1981.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, when -- I'm going to skip ahead a bit. When I asked him questions myself -- these are questions from the Prosecutor on this occasion. I asked him questions. He denied that as well, that he'd ever seen you in his house. Can you think of a reason why he's denying this contact with you? Unless, of course, he is a friendly operative?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He denied it. I will be very brief in my comment and very clear. He gave a false statement to this Tribunal about whether he had met me before or whether I had been in his house. He was worried about his own safety and the safety of his family. He was afraid of revenge, and he didn't tell the truth because he was afraid. I will tell you, even today many Albanians who were victims would probably apply to this Tribunal were they not afraid. I have information that some Albanians come to their houses and threaten them, telling them that if they come to the Tribunal, they will be killed and their houses will be set on fire. That's why the witness mentioned, the name of X, did not tell the truth, and maybe he was right. Well, I don't know, but that's his opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's your opinion, of course. Are you aware that X is a protected witness and had the ability to give evidence, as you have, in private? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that he was a protected witness, because as I said, I was not following the proceedings here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, he goes on in the answer, I've stopped halfway through it, he says this: "Dragan Jasovic was well known in Stimlje and Ferizaj as a dangerous inspector." Now, I asked you very carefully at the beginning about your reputation. Why would he be suggesting that about you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that he should have said that or, rather, he felt he had to say that, and I have explained why: for his own safety and the safety of his family. I'm convinced that he said this for the reason I have stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, he's asked a little more about this. "Can you tell us what you mean by that?" Is the question. "How was he well known as a dangerous inspector?" And he said, "Many citizens, Albanians, had been at his hands, had suffered at his hands. There were people who could tell you that they had difficulties at his hands, suffered. So in short, he was known as a dangerous person." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will say again. He said all this for the reasons I have explained. I don't recall the date, but I can tell you that two or three years ago, he contacted Bogoljub Janicevic, the former chief of the SUP, and told him that he wanted to come and testify before this Tribunal to tell the entire truth. And then Mr. Janicevic said to me, "I have spoken to Person X, and he sends his greetings." Everything he said here he said for the reason I have explained, because he was afraid for his own safety and the safety of his family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You see, he's never said that he's had to say all this to protect his family, in private session or anywhere else. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I follow, but I repeat, he didn't dare tell the real truth here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you dare to tell the real truth here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have come to this esteemed Tribunal with the desire to cooperate and to tell the real truth. I do not hail from a family that would bring me up to disseminate untruths, with due respect to all of you in this courtroom, apart from Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to just go on with this. We're dealing with July the 18th. He then says when he's asked about what happened in your office what that you asked a lot of questions about the KLA and people wearing uniforms of the KLA and Petrovo and so on, and he said he had to answer that he could not avoid answering, and he gave this rather longer explanation: "First of all, in his office there were two police sticks in his office that I saw." Did you have two police sticks in your office, or baseball bats or something like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ever since I went out of uniformed police, since 1986, I've been working as an inspector, and I never had any sticks, either truncheons or baseball bats or any manner of sticks in my office. But I reiterate, for all the reasons listed before, he had to say this. And certainly I will get in contact with him after this. We will spoke over the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you? Do you know his number, then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his telephone number, but Bogoljub Janicevic certainly I believe has his telephone number, the former chief of the secretariat of the interior in Urosevac. I believe he does have the number because they maintain frequent contacts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They maintain frequent contact because there's been a long-standing relationship?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated a minute ago, I did not have any sticks in my office. Secondly, what he stated is not correct. But again, my opinion is as I already stated, and that is my opinion, that he had to say that because of his and his family's safety. Because I know him. I know his father. There was no need to treat him or anybody else. And after all, I did not have any sticks in my office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you look at tab 26, Prosecution Exhibit 210. I'm going to deal with it in a global form. What he said about this statement was that the detail of it, starting under the word "Statement" on the first page and going through to the end, that the detail of that all came from you, and he merely Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. agreed. Is there any truth in that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question? I was reading the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. Instead of going through each sentence and saying -- and making the same comment, I'm dealing with it as a whole. His account was that the words and the details in the statement came from you wanting confirmation from him about these details and that basically they weren't --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In concrete terms --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could I just have a page reference, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just bear with me one moment. It's Day 27, and it's the cross-examination by Mr. Topolski, in fact, of this. And in mine it begins on page 44, 45, 46, 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. May I just go back to the question? I'm trying to encapsulate what Mr. Topolski put -- or asked of this witness. X claimed here that the content of this statement essentially came from you, and he merely endorsed it by saying yes but that it actually wasn't through other than the fact of the kidnapping itself. Do you follow what I've put to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do follow, but this is not correct what Person X said, because I did not know about the movements in the village of Petrovo. I could not imagine or concoct what was -- happened there, what he says here on the 16th of July at 2045, et cetera, et cetera. I asked him about the KLA in the village of Petrovo, and in connection to this, he spoke of his own volition. I can read through his statement what he said. He says: "Members of KLA came from Topilacka [phoen] and Granicka Reka [phoen], et cetera, et cetera." I cannot concoct this. This was his statement, his story, and it was not taken under duress. He related it himself. What I said, what is new in the village of Petrovo? Are there members of the KLA there? In this vein. I cannot remember exactly what sorts of things I asked him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I appreciate that. Now, you'll forgive me for not going through the whole statement, but I've dealt with it in principle. I want, in fact, now to pass to the next occasion that you saw him. Tab 27, Prosecution Exhibit 211, under seal, and it's behind the next tab. So -- or, rather, you'll have it as a separate document. You should have two -- two copies of this, the English version -- actually, there are three I think. Yes, three. So please follow it in whatever version you wish. I want to deal with rather carefully how he came to be in your office. And I'm going to start with dates first of all, some of which you've dealt with. The date on this official note, namely the date on which you are, as it were, recording what he's said in this version is the 5th of August. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, and that is the correct date. And it is true that we -- can I proceed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will have plenty at this of time to proceed on this. If there's anything you haven't covered by the time I've finished --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant specifically this interview -- Mr. Momcilo Sparavalo and I conducted that interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is our official note.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. In the note it is clear that he was seen by you on the 1st of August; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to carry this forward, I'd like you to look into the body of the statement. It's on our page 0 -- well, sorry, I can do it from the bottom. It may be quicker. It's not typed properly.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a statement. This is an official note.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I appreciate that. On the second page of the English version there is a date, the 25th of July, and I think you may find that in whatever version you're looking at as well. The 25th of July being the date at 12.00 that he says prisoners were made to line up in the prison yard. So I just want the date for the moment, 25th of July. Can you find that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to his statement, on the 25th of July at around 12.00, inmates were taken out into the yard and lined up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, if you would just care to just glance over the paragraph that comes below that, it's clear that what's describing or purporting to describe thereafter, eventually only the 25th later on, he starts at 12.00 noon, much later on he has the opportunity to escape. And this comes on the next page of the English version, 03066563, in the middle of the page. And you will also find it on the third page of your version, think.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my version?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Are you reading the English or are you reading the --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the Serbian?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Serbian version. Can you find the passage where he indicates that he has an opportunity to flee, the implication being on the 25th of July. Can you find that paragraph? It's on our third page. There's some -- certainly in our version it comes just underneath some bold type in which it is "In the name of the people you have been sentenced," and so on. It comes under that. Have you found the passage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean "In the name of the people you've been sentenced"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's just underneath that. He indicates that he uses an opportunity to flee. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted), when the time came to shoot in his direction a bullet jammed in his a rifle and" -- he named the person again -- "used his opportunity to flee."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I just want you to follow this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Before we move on, could we have a redaction please, for that name?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What line is that, please? We've picked it up, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, 34.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, without using the name if we can just concentrate on X all the time. Can I read it with you so we're sure we're talking about same thing. "Further in his account," this is you and your fellow officer writing out what he stayed, "X stated that running through the forest from the direction of Lapusnik he came to the Pristina-Pec main road and he gave himself up to policemen at a checkpoint in Komorane and recounted the incident to them, after which he was taken over by officials of the DB state security service in Pristina who conducted a detailed interview with him." Now, I want to take this in stages. You indicated to Mr. Black when he asked you the question, How do you know the way to Lapusnik, you said, Because X explained the route because part of it was the route he used to escape to the main road and the checkpoint. Do you remember saying that to Mr. Black? He's the Prosecutor to your right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. When -- went to Komorane with Person X, I asked him, Mr. X where are we going? It is the first time I went to that area. He told me which direction he came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, he's -- so you may be clear, again I asked him questions about this and again if a reference is wanted --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I -- this is not familiar territory. I remember him saying, I came from this direction fleeing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I appreciate what you're saying. Just bear with me. When I asked him questions -- I'm afraid I haven't got a day. This is just for others. You don't have this record. It's page 2416 onwards in the copy I have. I'm afraid I can't give a day for that, but I can specify it later if needed. I asked him questions carefully about this, and he said that none of this is true. He didn't go that way. He went a completely different way, across country to Ferizaj. Could you have been confused about what he was saying?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't have said that he came to Urosevac, because - how should I put it? - is south-east, and this in my opinion is coming from the north. But the fact is when I asked him, because Urosevac is in the opposite direction, he -- he would have been going towards the village of Crnoljevo. If he were to be Stimlje-bound, then he could encounter Komorane. We are talking about two different directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you think of any reason why he'd want to give a completely different version to this Tribunal to the one that he gave you both presumably when you interviewed him and when you took him to Lapusnik? Can you think of any reason why he'd give a completely different version?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can state here he came of his own accord, Mr. X, to report this case. He provided false testimony here for reasons of his and his family's safety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I want to suggest to you this hadn't got anything to do his family's safety even if that may be a reason on July the 18th. Can we just go on a little further with this? In this account that you've written down here, he is taken to Pristina -- well, there are two stages. He gives himself up to a policeman at a checkpoint and recounted the incident to them. Can we take that first of all? Did you ever -- when he never returned to sign his statement or even before then, did you ever check with any policeman at a checkpoint at Komorane about whether in fact he'd given them an account of what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, due to circumstances, when with Mr. X we came from Pristina to the -- to Komorane, due to circumstances, there was the same group that used to work on the checkpoint in the night when he reached this checkpoint in Komorane. And in a brief conversation with the policeman, they recounted that he said that he'd been kidnapped, taken to Lapusnik and managed to flee. Then state security officers took him away to process his statement. I'm not sure whether state security officers came to the Komorane checkpoint or whether he was driven by policemen there. So this is due to circumstances that we chanced upon the same group of policemen manning the checkpoint who were there when Mr. X came to report. Well, he didn't get there to report the case. He was fleeing and reached that checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that brings me to the second stage. Taken over by officials of the DB state security. Now, this is all on the 25th. Do you follow? Who conducted a detailed --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I follow. The 25th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, can you help us about where the detailed interview is that was conducted on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not known to me. I presume, that is my presumption, that it was conducted on the premises of state security offices in Pristina, but I don't know. Since we are talking about a grave crime of kidnapping, most probably state security officers did not conduct this interview out in the street. Neither would have I. By saying this, I mean to say I'm not sure where this interview took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate all of that. What I want to ask you is whether you ever followed that up and asked them for a copy of the interview they had had since you were yourself in contact with this person.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask that of them ever, because -- I don't know how to put it. Because they usually do not forward their statements to public security. It's a matter of procedure and arrangements between heads of public and state security. I would not venture to say why. In exceptional cases where charges are to be brought, et cetera.
